works.name: Big Waves: Five Decades of Surf Rock

podcast.title: Broad Influence and Legacy
podcast.body: Surf music is a significant genre with an influence and legacy that extends far beyond its beach-related origins. It can present in different forms, including punky or hardcore variations, and is associated with activities like skateboarding and snowboarding. The genre encompasses themes of guitars, amps, pedals, cars, girls, beer, and parties, and while it can feature vocals, it is often best experienced as instrumentals. "It's important and its influence and legacy goes way beyond the beach."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Building Block of Rock
podcast.body: Surf music is considered one of the foundational building blocks of punk rock, amplifier design, and recording studio innovations. "In fact, surf music could be considered one of the building blocks of punk rock, amplifier design and innovations in the recording studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Essential Role of Fender Stratocaster
podcast.body: With the consultation and influence of Dick Dale, the Fender Stratocaster became an indispensable component of the surf music sound. This collaboration helped define the genre's distinct sonic characteristics. "And with his help, the Fender Stratocaster became an essential part of that surf music sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 1

podcast.title: Origin Point: "Moon Dog"
podcast.body: Despite the general rule that there is never truly a "first" in music, historians of the Surf Music genre commonly point to The Gamblers' "Moon Dog" as the first surf music record. While twangy guitar instrumentals existed before it, "Moon Dog" is considered a strong candidate for marking the genre's beginning. "Historians of the Surf Music genre now generally point to it as the first Surf Music record ever, and it's as good a choice as any."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Persistence Through Decline
podcast.body: After a decline in the mid-1960s due to the rise of new rock genres like the British Invasion and psychedelic rock, surf music did not die out but continued to return and appear in interesting and important places over subsequent decades. "Surf music went into such a decline that even the Beach Boys started to diversify. But Surf did not die. It would return again and again over the coming decades."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Resurgence in Punk and New Wave
podcast.body: The "surf sound" or "surf feel" reappeared during the punk and new wave movements of the 1970s, indicating its infectious and fun nature. "It was just too much fun to play, which is one of the reasons the surf sound, or at least the surf feel, showed up during the punk and new wave explosions of the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Southern California Craze (Early 1960s)
podcast.body: The surf music craze originated in Southern California in the early 1960s. This genre predated the popular songs by bands like The Beach Boys, with artists like Dick Dale already innovating within the style. "By the early 1960s, the surf music craze had begun in Southern California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Worldwide Contemporary Scene
podcast.body: Contemporary surf music is a global phenomenon, with traditional and innovative groups found worldwide, including in Denmark, London, Japan, and Toronto, demonstrating its enduring appeal and adaptability. "Although it's been around since the 1950s, surf music is still very much with us. Some is still pretty traditional and sticks to the original rules of arrangement and performance. But then there are other groups who have done their best to advance the art of surf rock or bands that abuse surf as a big influence. And it's worldwide too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music
